stem: Best guess: which shareholder would make a corporation ineligible for S status?

choices.explanation: Individuals who are citizens are eligible.
Correct. Partnerships, C corporations, and nonresident aliens are ineligible shareholders.

explanation: Partnerships, C corporations, and nonresident aliens are ineligible shareholders.

stem: A calendar-year corporation eligible all year files Form 2553 on March 10, 2025 with all shareholders' consent. When is the S election effective?

choices.explanation: It was filed in time for 2025.
Elections are effective at the start of a tax year.
Timely elections are effective by rule.

explanation: An election made by the 15th day of the 3rd month is effective for the current year.

stem: An S corporation with no accumulated E&P distributes $40,000 to a shareholder whose stock basis (after the year's income) is $30,000. What does the shareholder recognize?

choices.explanation: The excess over basis is gain.
Correct. Tax-free up to basis (30,000); excess 10,000 is capital gain.

explanation: Tax-free up to basis (30,000); excess 10,000 is capital gain.

stem: Which feature would create a second class of stock and terminate S status?

choices.text: Voting and nonvoting common stock with identical distribution rights

choices.explanation: Correct. Differences in distribution or liquidation rights create a second class of stock.

choices.text: A shareholder that is an estate

explanation: Differences in distribution or liquidation rights create a second class of stock.

stem: A shareholder guarantees a $100,000 bank loan to her S corporation. What effect does the guarantee have on her basis?

choices.text: Basis increases by her ownership percentage of the loan

choices.explanation: A guarantee doesn't increase stock basis.

choices.text: No effect unless she actually pays on the guarantee
choices.explanation: Correct. S corporation debt basis requires a direct loan from the shareholder (unlike partnership liability sharing).

explanation: S corporation debt basis requires a direct loan from the shareholder (unlike partnership liability sharing).

stem: A former C corporation converted to S status in 2022 and sells an asset in 2025 that had a $50,000 built-in gain at conversion. What entity-level tax applies?
explanation: §1374: 21% on net recognized built-in gain within 5 years after conversion (the gain also passes through, reduced by the tax).

stem: An S corporation shareholder's stock basis is $20,000 at the start of 2025. Her share of ordinary income is $35,000 and of tax-exempt interest $2,000; she receives a $30,000 distribution. What is her ending stock basis?

choices.explanation: Omits tax-exempt income and the distribution.

explanation: Income items (including tax-exempt) increase basis before distributions reduce it.

stem: An S corporation with accumulated E&P of $15,000 and an AAA of $10,000 distributes $30,000 to its sole shareholder (stock basis $50,000). How is it treated?

choices.text: $10,000 tax-free (AAA), $15,000 dividend, $5,000 tax-free return of basis
choices.explanation: Correct. Ordering: AAA → accumulated E&P → remaining basis → gain.

explanation: Ordering: AAA → accumulated E&P → remaining basis → gain.

stem: How are an S corporation's items allocated when a shareholder sells stock mid-year (no election to close the books)?

choices.text: According to who owned stock at year-end
choices.explanation: Allocation is per share per day.

choices.text: Pro rata per share, per day

choices.explanation: S corporations allocate by shares and days.

explanation: §1377(a): per-share, per-day allocation.

stem: A 100% shareholder-employee of an S corporation takes no salary, only distributions. What is the IRS's likely position?

choices.text: Part of the distributions should be recharacterized as wages subject to payroll taxes
choices.explanation: Correct. Shareholder-employees must receive reasonable compensation for services.
Low salary doesn't terminate the election.
Dividend treatment isn't the issue here.

explanation: Shareholder-employees must receive reasonable compensation for services.

stem: An S corporation's election terminated in 2025. Absent IRS consent, when can it re-elect S status?

choices.explanation: Correct. §1362(g): a 5-year wait after termination unless the IRS consents.
It can re-elect after the waiting period.

explanation: §1362(g): a 5-year wait after termination unless the IRS consents.

stem: A 50% shareholder has stock basis of $8,000 and a $5,000 direct loan to the S corporation. Her share of the ordinary loss is $20,000. How much can she deduct?
explanation: Losses are deductible up to stock basis plus debt basis; the remaining 7,000 is suspended.

stem: When is Form 1120-S due for a calendar-year S corporation?

choices.explanation: Correct. S corporations file by the 15th day of the 3rd month.
That's the C corporation due date.
That's the extended C corporation date.

explanation: S corporations file by the 15th day of the 3rd month.

stem: A draft Form 1120-S reports ordinary business income of $90,000 after deducting $10,000 of charitable contributions and a $15,000 §179 expense, and after including $2,000 of savings account interest. What is the correct ordinary business income?

choices.explanation: This adds back the charity and §179 but leaves the portfolio interest in ordinary income.
This is the draft amount; three separately stated items are misclassified.
Correct. 90,000 + 10,000 + 15,000 − 2,000 = 113,000; the charity, §179 and interest are all separately stated.
This adds the interest back instead of removing it.

explanation: Items that could affect shareholders differently (charity, §179, portfolio income) are separately stated on Schedule K.

stem: Willow Inc., an S corporation, reports for 2025: gross receipts $800,000; cost of goods sold $300,000; salaries, including $120,000 to its sole shareholder, $250,000; depreciation $40,000; charitable contributions $10,000; long-term capital gain $15,000; dividend income $5,000. What is Willow's ordinary business income?

choices.explanation: That nets the separately stated items into ordinary income.
The shareholder's reasonable salary is deductible by the S corporation.
Correct. 800,000 − 300,000 − 250,000 − 40,000 = 210,000; charity, capital gain and dividends are separately stated.
Charitable contributions are separately stated, not deducted in ordinary income.

explanation: Ordinary business income excludes separately stated items (charitable contributions, capital gains, dividends). Shareholder-employee wages are deductible.

stem: Which S corporation item is reported to shareholders as ordinary business income rather than separately stated on Schedule K-1?

choices.explanation: Correct. Reasonable compensation is a deductible business expense in computing ordinary business income.

choices.text: Net §1231 gain on the sale of equipment
choices.explanation: §1231 gains and losses are separately stated.

choices.text: Interest income on a money market account

choices.explanation: §179 is separately stated and limited at the shareholder level.

explanation: Separately stated items are those whose character could affect a shareholder's tax (capital and §1231 gains, portfolio income, charity, §179). Wages to a shareholder-employee are ordinary deductions.

stem: How many shareholders may an S corporation have?

choices.explanation: Correct. Family members may count as one.

explanation: An S corporation may have up to 100 shareholders; members of a family may be treated as one shareholder.

stem: A nonresident alien buys shares in an S corporation. What is the effect?

choices.explanation: Any such shareholder terminates S status.

choices.text: He is taxed as a partner

choices.explanation: Correct. Nonresident aliens are ineligible shareholders.

explanation: Nonresident aliens can't be S shareholders; their ownership terminates the election.

stem: A calendar-year corporation wants S status effective for this year. By when must it file Form 2553?

choices.explanation: Correct. By the 15th day of the 3rd month.

explanation: An S election is effective for the current year if filed by the 15th day of the 3rd month of the tax year.

stem: An S corporation pays health insurance for a 10% shareholder-employee. How is it treated?

choices.text: W-2 wages; she may deduct it as an adjustment
choices.explanation: Correct. More-than-2% shareholders are treated like partners.

explanation: For a more-than-2% shareholder, premiums are included in W-2 wages, and the shareholder may claim the self-employed health insurance deduction.

stem: Which can be an S corporation shareholder?
explanation: Eligible shareholders include individuals (citizens or residents), estates and certain trusts and exempt organizations.

stem: Which S corporation item is separately stated to shareholders?

choices.explanation: Correct. Limits apply at shareholder level.

explanation: Items that may affect shareholders differently, like charitable contributions and capital gains, are separately stated.

stem: What tax year must an S corporation generally use?

choices.explanation: Correct. Unless a business purpose or §444 election applies.
That isn't what the rule says.

explanation: S corporations must use a calendar year unless they establish a business purpose or make a §444 election.

stem: What shareholder consent is needed to revoke an S election?
explanation: An S election may be revoked with consent of shareholders holding more than half of the shares.

stem: An S shareholder's debt basis was reduced by prior losses. This year the corporation has net income. What does the income restore first?
explanation: Net increases in basis first restore any reduction in debt basis before increasing stock basis.

stem: An S shareholder's beginning stock basis is $10,000. Her shares of items: ordinary income $4,000; distribution $8,000; nondeductible expenses $1,000; ordinary loss $7,000. How much loss is deductible?

choices.explanation: Correct. Income, then distributions, then nondeductible expenses, then losses.

explanation: Basis: 10,000 + 4,000 − 8,000 − 1,000 = 5,000 available for the loss; $2,000 is suspended.

stem: An S shareholder with $15,000 of suspended losses sells all her stock. What happens to the losses?

choices.explanation: Correct. Suspended losses don't transfer to the buyer.

explanation: Losses suspended for lack of basis are personal and are lost when the shareholder disposes of all her stock.

stem: An S corporation's AAA is $10,000. It has a $30,000 loss and makes a $5,000 distribution. What is its AAA at year-end?

choices.explanation: Distributions don't create a negative AAA.
Correct. Distributions can't push AAA below zero, but losses can.

explanation: AAA is adjusted for distributions before losses; losses may reduce AAA below zero.

stem: An S corporation distributes land (FMV $80,000; basis $50,000) to its shareholder. What is the effect?

choices.text: The corporation pays entity tax on the gain
$30,000 of gain passes through to her
choices.explanation: Correct. The corporation recognizes gain on appreciated property.

explanation: An S corporation recognizes gain on distributing appreciated property; it flows through, and the distribution reduces basis by FMV.

stem: An S corporation has voting and nonvoting common shares with identical distribution and liquidation rights. Does it violate the one-class-of-stock rule?

choices.explanation: Correct. Differences only in voting rights are allowed.
That isn't what the rule says.

explanation: Shares that differ only in voting rights are treated as one class of stock.

stem: A shareholder wants to hold S corporation stock in her traditional IRA. Is this permitted?

choices.explanation: Correct. Generally barred (bank stock is a narrow exception).

choices.text: Yes, if the IRA owns under 5%
Only if it's a Roth IRA

explanation: IRAs generally can't be S corporation shareholders; eligible trusts include QSSTs and ESBTs.

stem: On August 1, an S corporation's 101st shareholder is added. When does the election terminate?

choices.explanation: Correct. Termination occurs on the date of the disqualifying event.

explanation: An S election terminates on the day the corporation ceases to qualify.

stem: A shareholder's debt basis in a $20,000 loan was reduced to zero by losses. The corporation repays the note in full. What results?

choices.explanation: Correct. Repaying a reduced-basis loan produces gain.

explanation: Repayment of shareholder debt with reduced basis causes gain to the extent of the excess.

stem: An S corporation makes a $3,000 cash charitable contribution. How does it affect a 100% shareholder's stock basis?

choices.explanation: Correct. Separately stated deductions reduce basis.

choices.text: No effect; it isn't an ordinary loss

explanation: A shareholder's basis is reduced by her share of separately stated deductions, including charitable contributions.

stem: A corporation meant to elect S status for 2025 but filed Form 2553 in June 2025, late, with reasonable cause. What relief may be available?

choices.explanation: Correct. Relief is available within 3 years and 75 days.

choices.text: Only with a private letter ruling
Only if it had one shareholder

explanation: Rev. Proc. 2013-30 provides simplified relief for late S elections filed within 3 years and 75 days of the intended effective date.

stem: What is the maximum number of shareholders an S corporation may have?
explanation: An S corporation may have up to 100 shareholders, with family members treated as one.

stem: By when must Form 2553 be filed for an S election to take effect for the current year?

choices.explanation: That is too late to file.

choices.text: The last day of the year

choices.explanation: Correct. It's due 2 months and 15 days into the year.
That is too late to file.

explanation: Form 2553 must be filed by the 15th day of the 3rd month of the tax year (or anytime in the prior year).

stem: Which return does an S corporation file?
explanation: An S corporation files Form 1120-S and gives each shareholder a Schedule K-1.

stem: How long is the built-in gains recognition period after a C corporation converts to S status?

choices.explanation: Correct. The recognition period is 5 years.

explanation: Built-in gains recognized within 5 years of the S election are taxed at the corporate level.
